title: NOAA radio occultation → commercial data purchases (Spire, GeoOptics, PlanetiQ)
summary: NOAA has long obtained GNSS radio-occultation (RO) weather soundings from government-sponsored satellites: COSMIC/FORMOSAT-3, launched in 2006 under a US–Taiwan arrangement and decommissioned on 1 May 2020, and its follow-on COSMIC-2, launched in 2019 and still listed by NOAA as currently flying. Since 2016 NOAA has also bought RO data from private satellite operators, first through its Commercial Weather Data Pilot, which Congress codified in 2017, and from November 2020 for operational forecasts. The listed end date marks COSMIC-1's decommissioning; the public observing program continues, and commercial data supplements it rather than replacing it.

public.name: NOAA government-sponsored satellite radio-occultation observations (COSMIC/FORMOSAT-3, 2006–2020; COSMIC-2 from 2019)
public.funder: NOAA, with NASA, NSF, US Air Force and US Navy (COSMIC-1), in partnership with Taiwan's National Space Organization

private.name: Spire Global (with GeoOptics and PlanetiQ), commercial radio-occultation data contracts
funders: NOAA (Commercial Weather Data Pilot and Commercial Data Purchase appropriations)
private.outcome: Pilot contracts to GeoOptics and Spire (2016); two-year operational IDIQ contracts to GeoOptics and Spire with a $23 million ceiling (November 2020); NOAA began using purchased RO data in operational forecasts on 20 May 2021; follow-on RODB-2 IDIQ to PlanetiQ and Spire with a shared maximum of $59,312,954, ordering through March 2028.

claims.claim: NOAA has replaced its own radio-occultation satellites with commercial data.
claims.explanation: COSMIC-1 was decommissioned in May 2020, but its government-sponsored successor COSMIC-2 launched in 2019 and NOAA still lists it as currently flying. CRS describes commercial data as a complement to NOAA's systems. The 2017 Weather Act does let NOAA consider operational commercial purchases as an alternative to future NOAA space systems, so a larger future shift is permitted but has not replaced the public program.
